info.title: Calendly API (baton-calendly connector surface)
info.description:
Describes only the Calendly endpoints baton-calendly calls. Scope is derived from pkg/calendly/client.go; response shapes are derived from the structs in pkg/calendly/models.go and settled against Calendly's published OpenAPI document at https://developer.calendly.com/openapi/calendly-api.yaml (accessed 2026-09-23).

Only the properties the connector's structs declare are modelled. Calendly's document describes more per resource; the omissions are deliberate — spec scope is connector scope.

Paths are partly reconstructed. Calendly identifies every resource by an absolute URI (`https://api.calendly.com/organizations/{uuid}`), and the connector stores those URIs verbatim as its resource IDs. Three operations are therefore built by `url.Parse` or `url.JoinPath` on a stored URI rather than from a path template, and the templates below were recovered from Calendly's document.

Auth: a Calendly personal access or OAuth token sent as `Authorization: Bearer` by uhttp.NewBearerAuth.

Pagination: list responses carry a `pagination` object; the connector reads `next_page_token` and replays it as the `page_token` query parameter alongside `count`. A null token ends the loop.

Base URL: https://api.calendly.com by default, overridable via the connector's base-URL config.

servers.description: Calendly API v2. Default; overridable via the connector's base-url config.

tags.name: organization
tags.description: Organizations, their memberships, and pending invitations.

get.description:
Called first on every sync to discover which organization the token belongs to (pkg/connector/organizations.go:70), and as the first half of the connector's credential-validation probe (pkg/connector/connector.go:46).

`current_organization` is the organization URI that every other operation is scoped by — the connector stores it as its organization resource ID and feeds it back as the `organization` query parameter and as the base for the invitation paths. Parity-critical.

The path is built by formatting the literal `me` into the `/users/%s` template; the connector never fetches another user by ID.

Builds the connector's single organization resource (pkg/connector/organizations.go:75) and completes the credential-validation probe (pkg/connector/connector.go:51).

The client does not format this path. It calls `url.Parse` on the `current_organization` URI from getCurrentUser and requests it directly, so the base-URL config does not apply to this operation — the host comes from whatever Calendly returned. The template here was recovered from Calendly's document.

Calendly returns a `name` for multi-user organizations; the connector's struct does not declare it, so the organization resource is named from its URI instead.
get.x-connector-url-source: absolute URI from User.current_organization, not a formatted path

get.summary: List the memberships of an organization
get.description:
Source of the connector's user resources (pkg/connector/users.go:134) and of the organization role grants (pkg/connector/organizations.go:160). Also called with `email` set and no pagination when resolving a principal to the membership that must be deleted (pkg/connector/organizations.go:260).

`organization` is always sent — without it Calendly scopes the listing to the caller rather than the organization. `email` is sent only on the revoke path, where the connector passes the principal's display name, which for both user shapes it builds is the email address.

`user.uri` is the connector's user resource ID and `role` drives the role entitlement — both parity-critical. `uri` (the membership URI, not the user URI) is what deleteOrganizationMembership consumes, after `parseResourceID` trims it to its last path segment.

delete.summary: Remove a user from the organization
delete.description:
Backs revoking the `user` entitlement (pkg/connector/organizations.go:275). The `uuid` is the trailing segment of the membership URI found by the preceding filtered listOrganizationMemberships call — not the user's UUID.

The connector refuses to proceed if that lookup returns more than one membership, so a revoke is only issued when the email filter resolves to exactly one person.

Calendly returns 204 with no body. The client sends no body of its own but still attaches `null` — see the note on createRequest in the PR description.

get.description:
Source of the connector's pending-user resources (pkg/connector/users.go:112) and of the `pending_user` grants (pkg/connector/organizations.go:138). Also called with `email` set and no pagination when resolving a principal to the invitation that must be revoked (pkg/connector/organizations.go:284).

`status=pending` is hardcoded on every call and is load-bearing: Calendly returns accepted and declined invitations too when it is omitted, and the connector would emit already-accepted invitees as separate pending users alongside their real membership.

The path is built with `url.JoinPath` on the stored organization URI, so the base-URL config does not apply here either.

Note the identifier asymmetry this creates: users discovered through memberships are keyed by `user.uri`, but users discovered through invitations are keyed by `email`, because an unaccepted invitation has no user URI. The same person can therefore appear under two resource IDs across the two sources.
get.x-connector-url-source: url.JoinPath on the stored organization URI, not a formatted path

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Invitation status filter. The connector always sends `pending`; omitting it would also return accepted and declined invitations.

post.summary: Invite a user to the organization
post.description:
Backs granting the `pending_user` entitlement (pkg/connector/organizations.go:221). The email sent is the principal's resource ID, which for a pending user resource is the email address itself.

Calendly returns 201 with the created invitation; the client decodes nothing and keeps only the rate-limit headers.
post.x-connector-url-source: url.JoinPath on the stored organization URI, not a formatted path

email.description: Email address of the person being invited.

201.description: Invitation created. Body not decoded by the connector.

delete.description:
Backs revoking the `pending_user` entitlement (pkg/connector/organizations.go:296). The `uuid` is the trailing segment of the invitation URI found by the preceding filtered listOrganizationInvitations call.

Unlike the membership revoke, duplicates are tolerated here: the connector takes the first match rather than erroring, so a person with more than one pending invitation has only one revoked per call.

The path is built with `url.JoinPath` on the stored organization URI.
delete.x-connector-url-source: url.JoinPath on the stored organization URI, not a formatted path

bearerAuth.description: Calendly personal access token or OAuth access token, attached by uhttp.NewBearerAuth.

Error.description: Calendly error. The client decodes `title` and `message` and folds them into a gRPC Unknown status; the `details` array Calendly also returns is discarded.

OrgUuid.name: uuid
OrgUuid.description: The organization's UUID. Never formatted by the client — it arrives as part of the stored organization URI.

OrgUuidForInvitation.name: org_uuid
OrgUuidForInvitation.description: The organization's UUID, as Calendly names it on this path. Arrives as part of the stored organization URI.

MembershipUuid.name: uuid
MembershipUuid.description: The membership's UUID — the last path segment of `OrganizationMembership.uri`, extracted by parseResourceID. Not the user's UUID.

InvitationUuid.name: uuid
InvitationUuid.description: The invitation's UUID — the last path segment of `Invitation.uri`, extracted by parseResourceID.

OrganizationFilter.name: organization
OrganizationFilter.description: Organization URI to scope the listing to. Calendly documents this as optional, but the connector always sends it; without it the listing is scoped to the caller instead of the organization.

EmailFilter.name: email
EmailFilter.description: Restrict results to one email address. Sent only on the revoke paths, where the connector uses it to resolve a principal to a single membership or invitation.

Count.name: count
Count.description: Page size. The connector sends its configured resource page size, and omits the parameter entirely on the unpaginated revoke lookups — which means those fall back to Calendly's default of 20.

PageToken.name: page_token
PageToken.description: Page cursor, echoed from the previous response's `pagination.next_page_token`. Omitted on the first call and on the revoke lookups.

Pagination.description: Shared list envelope metadata. The connector decodes `count` and `next_page_token`; `next_page`, `previous_page`, and `previous_page_token` are returned by Calendly but not read.

count.description: Number of rows in this page.

next_page_token.description: Cursor for the next page, replayed as the `page_token` query parameter. Null when the collection is exhausted, which is what ends the connector's loop.

User.description: A Calendly user. Only the properties the connector decodes are listed.

uri.description: Canonical user URI. The connector's user resource ID for members discovered through memberships — parity-critical.

email.description: Email address. Used as the user's display name and login, and as the resource ID for users discovered through invitations.

name.description: Human-readable name. Split into first and last name for the user trait.

slug.description: Scheduling-page slug. Carried on the user profile.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp. Decoded into a plain Go string and parsed as RFC 3339; a parse failure is swallowed and the created-at trait is simply omitted.

current_organization.description: URI of the user's organization. Read only from getCurrentUser, where it becomes the connector's organization resource ID — parity-critical.

Organization.description: An organization. Only the properties the connector decodes are listed; Calendly also returns `name` and `kind`.

uri.description: Canonical organization URI. The connector's organization resource ID — parity-critical.

OrganizationMembership.description: A user's membership in an organization.

uri.description: Canonical membership URI. Its last path segment is the `uuid` for deleteOrganizationMembership — parity-critical.

organization.description: URI of the organization this membership belongs to.

role.description: The user's role in the organization. Maps one-to-one onto the connector's role entitlements. The connector hard-fails the sync on any value outside this enum, so an upstream role addition breaks syncing rather than degrading it.

user.description: The member's user record, embedded in full.

Invitation.description: An invitation to join an organization. The connector only ever sees pending ones.

uri.description: Canonical invitation URI. Its last path segment is the `uuid` for revokeOrganizationInvitation — parity-critical.

email.description: Invited email address. The connector's user resource ID for invitation-derived users — parity-critical.

status.description: Invitation status. Always `pending` in practice because the request pins the filter.

user.description: URI of the user who accepted the invitation. Decoded but empty for pending invitations, which is all the connector requests.

ErrorResponse.description: Calendly's error envelope, as far as the connector decodes it.

message.description: Human-readable message. The only field surfaced in the connector's error text.
